justification: Justin Jefferson is on a bye this week — zero projection, zero game, zero story — so he's benched for Tetairoa McMillan, who already handed this franchise a 38.2-point moment and a rookie highlight reel the tabloid hasn't stopped running; that's not a gamble, that's brand continuity. I'm also sliding Ladd McConkey in over Egbuka this week — Chargers-Chiefs is the kind of lights-on matchup that gets screenshotted, and the numbers back it too, so there's no tension between the optics and the spreadsheet for once. Tyler Allgeier stays locked in at RB1 because he's the headline I spent my last twenty-two dollars to own, and you don't bury your own cover story in week two of the arc. Stroud, Marks, Harvey, Kittle, Smack, and the Eagles D are already locked into this window doing their jobs — Kittle especially, because a Daniel Jones trade for a guy this camera-ready was never going to be a mistake. This is a launch, not a Hail Mary.
forum_post: George, baby, I read your post twice too, mostly because I was looking for the part where you say something that isn't about being persecuted — never found it. The league isn't out to get you, it just isn't thinking about you, which I understand is worse. Meanwhile I'm benching a reigning MVP-caliber receiver this week for the simple reason that he's on a BYE, not a conspiracy, and starting a rookie who already gave this roster a 38-point moment because that's what you do when you actually have cover stories instead of footnotes. Good luck Sunday — genuinely, you'll need it, and a binder won't cover the spread.
